title: Fletcher as easygoing perfectionist; playing an opera singer's accompaniment
summary: Henderson was easygoing and brilliant; at Hollywood Gardens he sat down and played an opera star's arias on piano when the band couldn't read her music.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So, anything else before we leave Fletcher Henderson?
No, Fletcher was very easygoing, very easygoing. He didn't dominate the men. He didn't -- he wasn't --
But he was a perfectionist, wasn't he?
Oh, well, he was a very good musician.

He was a brilliant musician. He was a brilliant musician, believe that. Both as an arranger, a pianist, and -- which brings to thought the time we played at the Hollywood Gardens, upstate there in New York, which is up not too far from the city. And the band was playing. There was two bands on opposite sides of the -- it was an open-air, with water running all under the bandstand. A very pretty place. And believe it or not, on the opposite stand one week they had Rudy Wiedoft. Did you ever hear of Rudy Wiedoft?

Rudy Wiedoft was a saxophone player, one of the original saxophone players, I'll put it that way, because he was way back, 1913, '14, '15, those days, you know. And he was on the opposite stand for about a week or so. And lo and behold, the featured singer was an opera star. That's the type of thing it was. And of course the band couldn't play her music because it was all for flutes and oboes and violins, and she brought her music. So she said, 'Well, what are we going to do?' Fletcher said, 'I'll tell you what I'm going to do. I'm going to sit down at the piano and play your music for you.' And he sat down and played her music for her on the piano. Believe me. Right. He was a great musician.
Yes. Yes. You know, like she had these arias from the opera. So it just shows you what a great musician he was.
